name: The Ulster Cycle (Rúraíocht)
dom: heroic saga; the Ulaid; the Táin
note: Medieval Irish heroic-tale corpus centred on the Táin Bó Cúailnge; hub collective for the Ulster heroes. Attested in the Book of the Dun Cow and Book of Leinster.

name: The Fenian/Ossianic Cycle (Fiannaíocht)
dom: heroic saga; the fian; Fionn and the Fianna
note: Cycle of tales of Fionn mac Cumhaill and the Fianna; hub collective. Attested from Acallam na Senórach onward.

name: Irish Folklore Beings
dom: fairy-belief; otherworld beings; the síde
note: Hub grouping for post-medieval Irish folk supernatural beings collected in the folklore record (Ó hÓgáin).

name: Cú Chulainn
dom: warrior; champion of Ulster; the ríastrad (warp-spasm)
note: Central hero of the Ulster Cycle; son/earthly aspect of the god Lugh. Attested throughout the Táin (Kinsella).

name: Conchobar mac Nessa
dom: king of the Ulaid; Emain Macha
note: Legendary king of Ulster at Emain Macha in the Ulster Cycle.

name: Medb
dom: queen of Connacht; sovereignty; instigator of the Táin
note: Queen of Connacht whose cattle-raid drives the Táin; carries sovereignty-goddess overtones (Kinsella; Ó hÓgáin).

name: Fergus mac Róich
dom: exiled Ulster champion; virility
note: Former king of Ulster exiled to Connacht, a leading warrior of the Táin.

name: Deirdre
dom: tragic heroine; Longes mac nUislenn
note: Heroine of 'The Exile of the Sons of Uisliu', a remscél of the Táin.

name: Scáthach
dom: warrior-woman; martial instructor; Alba/Skye
note: Warrior-woman who trains Cú Chulainn and grants the gáe bolga (Tochmarc Emire).

name: Emer
dom: wife of Cú Chulainn; the six gifts
note: Wife of Cú Chulainn, wooed in Tochmarc Emire.

name: Fionn mac Cumhaill
dom: fian-leader; seer; the salmon of knowledge
note: Central hero of the Fenian Cycle, leader of the Fianna (Ó hÓgáin).

name: Oisín
dom: poet-warrior; Tír na nÓg
note: Son of Fionn, poet of the Fianna and namesake of the Ossianic Cycle; visits Tír na nÓg.

name: Diarmuid Ua Duibhne
dom: fian warrior; the love-spot (ball seirce)
note: Fenian warrior and foster-son of Aengus; elopes with Gráinne.

name: Gráinne
dom: heroine; betrothed of Fionn; the elopement
note: Daughter of Cormac mac Airt who elopes with Diarmuid (Tóraigheacht Dhiarmada agus Ghráinne).

name: Partholón
dom: invasion leader; second settlement of Ireland
note: Leader of the second invasion of Ireland in the Lebor Gabála Érenn.

name: Cesair
dom: first settler of Ireland; pre-Flood arrival
note: Granddaughter of Noah and leader of the first (pre-Flood) settlement in the Lebor Gabála Érenn.

name: Nemed
dom: invasion leader; ancestor of later peoples
note: Leader of the third invasion and ancestor of the Fir Bolg and Tuatha Dé in the Lebor Gabála Érenn.

name: The Milesians (Sons of Míl / Meic Míled)
dom: final invasion; Gaelic ancestors of the Irish
note: The Gaels, sons of Míl Easpáine, who take Ireland from the Tuatha Dé in the Lebor Gabála Érenn.

name: Tuan mac Cairill
dom: shapeshifting survivor; witness to the invasions
note: Sole survivor of Partholón's people who lives through many animal forms and recounts the invasions (Scel Tuain).

name: Fintan mac Bóchra
dom: shapeshifting sage; the salmon; long memory
note: Husband of Cesair who survives the Flood and ages through the eras as a witness-sage (Lebor Gabála; dindshenchas).

name: The Cailleach (Cailleach Béirre)
dom: winter; land-shaping; sovereignty; old age
note: Sovereignty/landscape hag-goddess of winter and the Irish/Scottish-Gaelic countryside (Ó hÓgáin).

name: Tailtiu
dom: earth/land-clearing; sovereignty; Lughnasa
note: Foster-mother of Lugh whose funeral games at Teltown founded the Lughnasa assembly (dindshenchas).

name: Carman
dom: eponymous goddess; the óenach assembly
note: Fomorian-allied sorceress and eponym of the Carman assembly in Leinster (dindshenchas).

name: Tlachtga
dom: eponymous goddess; the Hill of Ward; Samhain fire
note: Daughter of the druid Mug Ruith, eponym of Tlachtga (Hill of Ward) and its Samhain assembly (dindshenchas).

name: The Aos Sí (the síde / fairy folk)
dom: otherworld folk; the síde mounds; the diminished gods
note: The fairy folk of the síde, understood as the diminished Tuatha Dé Danann; the encompassing class of Irish supernatural beings (Ó hÓgáin).

name: The Banshee (bean sí)
dom: death-omen; keening; the lament
note: 'Woman of the síde' whose keening foretells a death in certain families (Ó hÓgáin).

name: The Leprechaun (luprachaín)
dom: solitary fairy; shoemaker; hidden gold
note: Solitary fairy cobbler guarding hidden treasure in Irish folklore (Ó hÓgáin).

name: The Púca
dom: shapeshifting spirit; mischief; the Samhain blight
note: Shapeshifting Irish nature-spirit, often a black horse, both helpful and malicious (Ó hÓgáin).

name: The Dullahan
dom: headless rider; death-herald
note: Headless horseman of Irish folklore who heralds death (Ó hÓgáin).

name: The Changeling (iarlais)
dom: fairy substitution; the stolen child
note: Fairy substitute left in place of a human (often an infant) stolen by the síde (Ó hÓgáin).
